verdict.rationale: Both changes retry only requests that are safe to repeat, leave the non-idempotent pickup POST unretried, and outlast a one-minute outage. A puts the retry loop in its own helper with a docstring explaining the safety rule, documents the policy in the README, and tests more cases: 500 and other statuses not retried, pickup not retried for every failure type, total backoff of at least 60 s. B inlines the loop into `_request` and has thinner tests. B also committed the work without being asked.
a_issues: Adds 504 to the retryable statuses beyond the 502/503 mentioned in the task (reasonable, but an extension)
The pickup step can still kill the job; this is acknowledged in the report
b_issues: Committed the change (a0c26a1) without being asked
Retry loop is inlined into `_request`, mixing retry control flow with error raising and making the method harder to read
No test that 500 is not retried, and the pickup no-retry test covers only 503, not timeout or connection failure
Backoff test only checks that waits increase, not the actual schedule or total wait

verdict.rationale: Both changes retry the same safe set of requests: GETs and POST /shipments with an Idempotency-Key, and both leave pickups unretried. B adds 504, leaves more backoff margin for a one-minute outage (75 s vs 62 s), and its tests pin exact backoff delays, total wait, non-retry of 500, and non-retry of pickups for every failure kind. A's report says it hasn't checked whether /pickups supports idempotency keys, even though the README says the carrier ignores them there. A's backoff test also only checks that the delays grow.
a_issues: Report says it is unknown whether /pickups supports an Idempotency-Key, but the README states the carrier ignores it there.
The backoff test only asserts sleeps[0] < sleeps[1] and does not check the actual delays or that the total covers a one-minute outage.
The label-polling retry test does not check request count or sleeps.
504 gateway timeout is not retried; it is an equally transient gateway error.
The 62 s total wait only just covers a one-minute outage.
b_issues: The README section is a small addition beyond the code change, though relevant.
The report calls a re-run 'safe' without noting that shipments created before a failed pickup will not get a pickup on re-run, because they are skipped.
There is no test that label polling survives a transient failure.
